text:
New Jersey arrives on a four-game winning streak, the latest a 5-4 overtime win at NYI last night after trailing by two goals, with Jack Hughes scoring the winner. Toronto has gone 1-4-0 in its last five, falling 4-2 to MTL, and is without Kirill Marchenko (lower body, on injured reserve), Nick Blankenburg and Marshall Rifai. Both teams are on the second night of a back-to-back, so the tired legs are shared.

Our numbers favor the Devils. At five on five, NJD has taken 59% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in its games, TOR 46%. We project NJD for 3.53 goals tonight, TOR for 2.84. Toronto's penalty kill allows 0.80 expected goals a game against a New Jersey power play that creates 0.81, and the Leafs take 4.3 penalties a game. In net, Anthony Stolarz (projected) is at +2.3 goals saved above expected this season but -6.6 last year, while Connor Hellebuyck (projected) is at -0.5 after a +3.4 season in 2025-26's predecessor year.

Watch Jack Hughes, at 44% to score and 81% for a point, and Auston Matthews, at 38% and 70% on a six-game point streak. With Marchenko out, Easton Cowan has moved beside Matthews's line and William Nylander is up to 21:34 a night. Our under-the-radar picks are Anthony Mantha, 24% to score thanks to dangerous recent shots, and Luke Hughes, 51% for a point with his ice time up.
